ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Chen, MD
Department: Urology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
He and his partner have been attempting to conceive for the past 10 months without success. He reports regular intercourse and denies any known sexually transmitted infections or previous genitourinary surgeries.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He and his partner have been attempting to conceive for the past 10 months without success. He reports regular intercourse and denies any known sexually transmitted infections or previous genitourinary surgeries. His menses-tracking app indicates his partner has regular cycles. On further questioning, he reveals that he is a competitive bodybuilder and follows a strict high-protein diet and intense resistance training regimen. He has gained a significant amount of muscle mass over the past two years, which he attributes to disciplined training and supplementation. He admits to using "performance enhancers" obtained online but is vague on the specific substances. He has noticed increased acne over his face and back, along with occasional mood swings. His libido is normal, and he has no difficulty achieving erections. He shaves his chest and arms but says his body hair growth has noticeably increased. His voice is deep, and he denies gynecomastia, testicular pain, or changes in testicle size,

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
The patient has no significant past medical history

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- No prior surgeries

MEDICATIONS:
He takes no prescription medications.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with history of left-sided varicocele
- Paternal uncle with male factor infertility
- Mother with hypothyroidism

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker (denies tobacco use). Alcohol: None (denies alcohol consumption). Occupation: Personal trainer and amateur competitive bodybuilder.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Though on exam his testicles appear small for age. Scrotal exam reveals no masses or varicoceles.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-03-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Okafor, MD
Department: Urology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive left-sided groin discomfort and difficulty conceiving with his partner after 2 years of unprotected intercourse. He reports the pain is usually dull and denies any history of trauma or urinary complaints.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns for follow-up of infertility with new left-sided groin discomfort. He reports that the pain is usually dull. He has no history of trauma, urinary complaints, or recent infections.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Exogenous androgen use (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
He has never had surgery

MEDICATIONS:
He does not take medications

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with history of left-sided varicocele
- Paternal uncle with male factor infertility
- Mother with hypothyroidism

SOCIAL HISTORY:
He denies alcohol, tobacco, or illicit drug use

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, he appears healthy, with normal secondary sexual characteristics and symmetric testicular size. Inspection of the genitalia shows no erythema, swelling, or visible masses.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies reveal normal testosterone and follicle-stimulating hormone levels.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
During the examination, the clinician suspects an abnormality of the pampiniform plexus and considers a bedside maneuver that can accentuate venous dilation.
